How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to **generate a RESTful API request** for the *“Get information of device connector versions”* endpoint in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. I’ll cover: 1. Where to find the endpoint in the UI 2. How to generate the request (cURL, Postman, Swagger UI) 3. Authentication (Bearer token) 4. Example request & response 5. Using the `requests_get` helper (Python) --- ## 1. Locate the Endpoint in the Dashboard UI | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Log in to the Cisco Nexus Dashboard web UI. | | 2 | In the left‑hand navigation pane, click **API Explorer** (or **Developer Tools → API Explorer**). | | 3 | In the search box, type **“device connector versions”** or **“connector‑versions”**. | | 4 | The endpoint will appear as something like:
`GET /api/v1/device-connectors/{connectorId}/versions` | | 5 | Click the endpoint to open its details. | > **Tip:** If you’re not sure of the exact path, the UI will show the full URL pattern and any required path/query parameters. --- ## 2. Generate the Request ### A. Using the “Generate Request” Button (cURL) 1. In the endpoint details page, click **“Generate Request”**. 2. The UI will display a ready‑to‑copy cURL command, e.g.: ```bash curl -X GET "https:///api/v1/device-connectors/12345/versions" \ -H "accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` 3. Copy the command and paste it into your terminal or a script. ### B. Using “Try it out” (Swagger UI) 1. Click **“Try it out”**. 2. Fill in the required parameters (e.g., `connectorId`). 3. Click **“Execute”**. 4. The UI will show the raw request and the JSON response. ### C. Using Postman 1. Create a new **GET** request. 2. Set the URL to `https:///api/v1/device-connectors/{connectorId}/versions`. 3. In the **Headers** tab, add: - `accept: application/json` - `Authorization: Bearer ` 4. Hit **Send**. --- ## 3. Authentication Cisco Nexus Dashboard uses **Bearer Token** authentication. | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Obtain a token via the auth endpoint (usually `POST /api/v1/auth/token`). | | 2 | Example request: | ```bash curl -X POST "https:///api/v1/auth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"username":"admin","password":"YourPassword"}' ``` | Response | Example | |----------|---------| | `access_token` | `"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."` | | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 3 | Use the returned token in the `Authorization` header of your API calls. | > **Note:** Tokens usually expire after 30–60 minutes. Refresh them as needed. --- ## 4. Example Request & Response ### Request ```bash curl -X GET "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v1/device-connectors/98765/versions" \ -H "accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." ``` ### Response (JSON) ```json { "connectorId": "98765", "versions": [ { "versionId": "v1.0.0", "releaseDate": "2023-01-15", "status": "stable", "notes": "Initial release." }, { "versionId": "v1.1.0", "releaseDate": "2023-04-20", "status": "beta", "notes": "Added support for new protocols." } ], "pagination": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 20, "totalPages": 1, "totalItems": 2 } } ``` > **Optional Query Parameters** (if supported): > `?page=1&pageSize=20&sort=releaseDate&filter=status:stable` --- ## 5. Using the `requests_get` Helper (Python) If you prefer to fetch the JSON directly from a script, you can use the provided `requests_get` function. Replace `` with the full endpoint URL (including any query parameters). ```python from functions import requests_get url = "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v1/device-connectors/98765/versions" params = {} # Add query params here if needed response = requests_get({ "url": url, "params": params }) print(response) # This will print the JSON response ``` > **Important:** The helper assumes you have already set up authentication (e.g., by adding an `Authorization` header in the request). If the helper does not support headers directly, you may need to extend it or use the standard `requests` library. --- ## Quick Checklist - [ ] **Login** to the Dashboard UI. - [ ] **Navigate** to API Explorer → find the “device connector versions” endpoint. - [ ] **Generate** the cURL or use “Try it out”. - [ ] **Obtain** a Bearer token (if you don’t have one). - [ ] **Add** the `Authorization` header. - [ ] **Execute** the request and review the JSON response. Feel free to adapt the example URLs, headers, and parameters to match your environment. If you run into any specific errors (e.g., 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found), double‑check the token, endpoint path, and required parameters. Happy API‑calling!
